name: Notion Forms
description: Notion Forms is a database view for collecting requests, feedback, surveys, RSVPs, and other structured responses inside a Notion workspace. Form questions map to database properties, submissions become database pages, and customers can configure sharing, anonymity, conditional logic, automations, and response analysis.
agentUseSummary: Do not create a separate Notion Forms connection or install. Use the canonical Notion provider for its currently approved bounded page and content actions. Relay does not create or configure form views, publish form links, impersonate respondents, submit public forms, change response permissions, or manage form automations; those remain explicit Notion product workflows even though Notion's Views API now identifies form views and exposes a limited configuration subset.

blocked.label: Create a Notion Forms connection
blocked.description: Forms are views on Notion databases and use the same workspace identity, content capabilities, page resources, permissions, and OAuth lifecycle as canonical Notion.

blocked.label: Install duplicate Forms tools
blocked.description: Relay mounts supported Notion content operations once through the canonical provider rather than publishing parallel form credentials, policies, actions, and audit state.

blocked.label: Configure form views
blocked.description: Creating, retrieving, renaming, filtering, sorting, opening, closing, updating, or deleting form views and their questions, properties, descriptions, presentation, conditional logic, and response settings is outside Relay's current Notion V1 contract.

blocked.label: Publish or share forms
blocked.description: Changing workspace-only or public access, copying or distributing form URLs, embedding forms, changing anonymity, branding, respondent access, or Enterprise web-sharing controls is blocked.

blocked.label: Submit a form
blocked.description: Relay does not fill public or private forms, bypass login or required questions, impersonate anonymous or named respondents, or treat ordinary database page creation as a form submission.

blocked.label: Administer responses and workflows
blocked.description: Bulk response access, export, deletion, charts, filters, notifications, automations, downstream Slack or status actions, and high-volume response administration remain outside this alias.

blocked.label: Use private Notion interfaces
blocked.description: Sessions, cookies, passwords, verification codes, browser automation, scraping, undocumented endpoints, arbitrary form links, untyped view operations, and raw requests are blocked.

approvalProfiles.label: Use Notion
approvalProfiles.description: No separate Notion Forms action is enabled because Forms is a database view governed by the canonical Notion connection and product UI.

runtimeSupport.description: No duplicate Notion Forms tools are mounted. OpenClaw uses canonical Notion only for its approved bounded shared-content workflows.
No duplicate Notion Forms tools are mounted. Hermes uses canonical Notion only for its approved bounded shared-content workflows.

providerSetup.blocker: Notion Forms is a form-type view on a Notion database, not a distinct identity, provider, token, callback, or resource system. Notion's current Views API can list and retrieve views and can create, update, or delete a form view using the same Notion content capabilities; its form-specific configuration covers open or closed state, anonymous submissions, and respondent permissions. The product surface is broader: questions map to database properties and includes public or workspace link sharing, descriptions, conditional logic, branding, response pages, automations, charts, and administrative controls. Relay's canonical Notion V1 deliberately exposes bounded page and block workflows while blocking database schema, sharing, public publishing, destructive changes, raw APIs, and untyped view administration. A separate Forms connector would duplicate authority and would not safely represent the complete product lifecycle.
providerSetup.nextAction: Keep this product-mode slug non-installable and use canonical Notion only for its currently approved explicit shared-page and block actions; do not label ordinary page creation as a form response. Customers must create, customize, publish, close, and administer forms and responses in Notion. If Relay later adds form support, extend the canonical Notion provider rather than this alias and freeze a typed form-view contract covering database and data-source binding, question and property mapping, open and anonymous state, submission permissions, public-link and Enterprise restrictions, response access, Safe approvals and Dangerous behavior, deletion and rollback, automation side effects, sensitive-data classification, audit, pagination, and production acceptance.

evidence.supports: Notion describes Forms as an integrated workspace feature with database-backed responses, public or private sharing, embeds, question customization, anonymous submissions, conditional logic, and automation triggers.

Notion documents form views, property-backed questions, required database access, web and workspace sharing, respondent permissions, response pages, automations, high-volume considerations, and desktop or web configuration.

Notion's Views API recognizes form views and documents bounded form configuration for closed state, anonymous submissions, and respondent permissions under the canonical Notion bearer-token and content-capability model.

Notion documents creating a form-type view on explicit database and data-source identifiers with insert and update content capabilities, confirming that Forms uses canonical Notion resources rather than separate provider authority.

Notion documents permanent view deletion under update-content capability and rejects deleting the final database view, supporting Relay's decision to keep destructive view administration outside this alias.
